**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Section 7.2, first instance (p0026)**

- **Issue:** "Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives." This binds *us*, not Vendor, and functions as a right of first refusal / MFC-style restraint — de facto exclusivity with no product-category limit, no time limit, and no exit for Vendor performance failure.
- **Conflict:** Section 12.3 has Vendor acknowledge that Customer has made "no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment."
- **Redline (validated, preferred position):** delete Section 7.2 in full. Fallback offered in the comment: at most a non-binding courtesy notice, limited to a defined service category and 12 months, terminating automatically on any Vendor service-level or delivery failure.
- **Noted but not flagged here:** Section 2.1's three-year, USD 2M take-or-pay commitment reinforces the same lock-in and also contradicts 12.3 — a minimum-volume issue for the separate commitment rule.
